audits.title: The effectiveness of a multifaceted, group-facilitated audit and feedback intervention to increase tranexamic acid use during total joint arthroplasty.
audits.standard: Evidence-based guidelines and local practice protocols supporting tranexamic acid as standard of care in THA and TKA

cycle1.result: TXA use 66.6% for THA and 62.4% for TKA.

audits.intervention: Two individual data reports on TXA use and transfusion compared with peers, plus a group-facilitated feedback session

cycle2.result: TXA use 74.4% for THA (absolute change 7.9%, 95% CI 2.4 to 13.3) and 82.3% for TKA (absolute change 19.9%, 95% CI 15.0 to 25.0).

audits.other_findings: Dosing also shifted towards evidence-based practice guidelines.
audits.citation: Gjata I, Olivieri L, Baghirzada L, Endersby RVW, Solbak NM, Weaver CGW, et al.. The effectiveness of a multifaceted, group-facilitated audit and feedback intervention to increase tranexamic acid use during total joint arthroplasty. Can J Anaesth. 2022;69(9):1129-1138. doi:10.1007/s12630-022-02236-x. PMID: 35877041.

audits.title: Improving Adherence to National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for the Use of Tranexamic Acid in Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.standard: NICE: combined topical and intravenous tranexamic acid in knee arthroplasty for patients without renal impairment (1 g IV only with significant renal impairment)
audits.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics Department, Good Hope Hospital, University Hospitals Birmingham (elective surgical hub)

cycle1.result: TXA used in 20 (48.8%), not used in 21 (51.2%); combined IV and topical 3 (7.3%); IV only 14 (34.1%); topical only 3 (7.3%).

audits.intervention: Targeted emails to consultants and registrars, presentation at a specialty meeting, and posters on TXA and NICE guidance on computers across the elective surgical suite.

cycle2.result: TXA used in 38 (73.1%) (p=0.016), not used in 14 (26.9%); combined IV and topical 16 (30.8%) (p=0.005); IV only 22 (42.3%).

audits.other_findings: In cycle 2 non-use was 20% (8/40) without a tourniquet versus 50% (6/12) with one. In significant renal impairment TXA was omitted in 8/9 (cycle 1) and 6/12 (cycle 2).
audits.citation: Hamed A, Hamid MA, Lawrence C, Sherif IA, Younis Z. Improving Adherence to National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guidelines for the Use of Tranexamic Acid in Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Quality Improvement Initiative. Cureus. 2024;16(12):e76111. doi:10.7759/cureus.76111. PMID: 39835043.

audits.title: Improving Perioperative Tranexamic Acid Administration in Hip Fracture Surgery: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project at Dorset County Hospital.
audits.standard: NICE guideline: offer TXA to adults having surgery expected to cause moderate blood loss (>500 ml)
audits.setting: Dorset County Hospital, Dorchester; district general hospital

cycle1.result: 26/37 (70.0%) eligible patients received intraoperative TXA; contraindication documented in 0%

audits.intervention: Local hip fracture protocol updated to include TXA, targeted teaching for anaesthetic and theatre staff, and encouragement to record contraindications

cycle2.result: 23/27 (85.2%) received TXA; contraindication documented in 7.4%; difference not significant (Fisher's exact p = 0.23, OR 0.41)

audits.other_findings: No thromboembolic complications in either cycle; transfusion and outcome data were not collected.
audits.citation: Mahmoud ME, Mustafa Q, Mitchell O. Improving Perioperative Tranexamic Acid Administration in Hip Fracture Surgery: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project at Dorset County Hospital. Cureus. 2025;17(12):e98220. doi:10.7759/cureus.98220. PMID: 41480472.

audits.title: Electronic patient blood management monitoring using routine health record data: A proof-of-principle study monitoring perioperative tranexamic acid use.
audits.standard: NICE Quality Standard QS138 statement 2 (pre-2026 definition): adults having surgery with expected blood loss >500 mL should receive perioperative tranexamic acid
audits.setting: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, single academic tertiary centre (four hospital sites); automated EHR-based audit

cycle2.result: Overall automated TXA compliance 86.3% (manual QI audit same period 90%, 10 cases); trauma and orthopaedics 98.2% (n = 393), cardiac surgery 83.7%, gynaecology 83.2%, urology 94.2%, colorectal 43.5%, vascular 0%. Improvement from 2024 included gynaecology +26.8% and cardiac surgery +15.6%.

audits.other_findings: Paper is mainly a validation of an automated audit: denominator coverage 96.2%, miscoding 3.9%, WHO checklist–EPR concordance 74.2%, and manually adjudicated 'true' compliance 85.3%. Primary hip and knee replacements 98.8%, revision hip and knee 100%, neck of femur fracture fixation 96.7%; open iliofemoral and aortic operations 0%.
audits.citation: Che Rahimi MN, Polzella P, Amin M, Bakhishli G, Godley S, Murphy MF, et al.. Electronic patient blood management monitoring using routine health record data: A proof-of-principle study monitoring perioperative tranexamic acid use. Transfusion. 2026;66(8):1506-1519. doi:10.1111/trf.70270. PMID: 42154518.

audits.title: Use of tranexamic acid in trauma patients requiring massive transfusion protocol activation: an audit in a major trauma centre in New Zealand.
audits.standard: International best practice for TXA in severe trauma: initial dose within three hours of injury and second dose
audits.setting: Major trauma centre, Canterbury District Health Board, Christchurch

cycle1.result: 76.2% of indicated patients received an initial TXA dose and 19.0% both doses; 21.1% dosed within one hour, 52.6% between one and three hours, 26.3% after three hours.

audits.citation: Chapman N. Use of tranexamic acid in trauma patients requiring massive transfusion protocol activation: an audit in a major trauma centre in New Zealand. N Z Med J. 2018;131(1483):8-12. PMID: 30286060.

audits.title: Strategies for increasing the use of tranexamic acid in patients undergoing major surgery.
audits.standard: Joint Royal Colleges Tranexamic Acid in Surgery Implementation Group recommendations (October 2022) for surgery with potential blood loss >500 ml
audits.setting: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Tranexamic acid used in 50 of 100 (50%) major surgical cases.

audits.intervention: Dissemination of Joint Royal Colleges guidance, education sessions, and a tranexamic acid prompt added to the local WHO surgical checklist.

cycle2.result: Tranexamic acid used in 65 of 96 (68%) cases.

audits.other_findings: Three audit cycles; continuous monitoring showed a sustained shift in practice.
audits.citation: Murphy L, Warnakulasuriya SR. Strategies for increasing the use of tranexamic acid in patients undergoing major surgery. Anaesth Rep. 2024;12(2):e12335. doi:10.1002/anr3.12335. PMID: 39610470.
